resources.title: Breathing
resources.summary: Learn why 20,000 daily breaths matter, the common dysfunctions that throw breathing off, and the three areas (diaphragmatic, costal, and 360 breathing) to focus on for better oxygenation.
resources.body:
---

[youtube:ldNnKVGxabA]

> 💡 Breathing is one of the most essential functions we perform every day, often without even thinking about it. But have you ever stopped to consider how you breathe? Interesting fact: We each take approximately 20,000 breaths every single day.

#### Let's start with a quick exercise:

- Take a deep breath in. Do you feel like you are getting a little taller? If not, you may have been breathing wrong.

- Breathing wrong is when you use your neck and shoulders to lift your thoracic cavity.

- Most children under the age of 5 breathe properly, so what happens?

  - Long hours of sitting (at school, in a car, or at work)

  - Injuries to the midline of the body during sports (during your childhood days)

  - Wearing waistbands, bra straps, or compression garments

- A good breath involves expanding 360 degrees around the rib cage, and your neck should not move.

Taking a moment to pay attention to your breath can have a significant impact on your physical and mental wellbeing. Did you know that poor breathing mechanisms are the most common cause of neck and shoulder pain? If you experience frequent neck and shoulder pain, maybe it's your breathing.

But don't worry, in this article, we'll explore the world of breathing with interactive ways to help you identify and treat dysfunctions, and breathing techniques that can improve your overall health and wellbeing. We'll cover the mechanics of breathing, types of breathing methods, and even common dysfunctions that can affect the way we breathe.

So, whether you're looking to improve your posture, reduce stress and anxiety, or simply breathe more efficiently, read on to discover the world of breathing. You'll be amazed at how much you can learn about this fundamental aspect of our lives.

![Feeling the constant need to do this? Hmm you might want to look into your breathing 😮‍💨 ](/assets/img/resources/breathing-1.jpg)

#### So why is it important to breathe properly?

- **Efficient cardiovascular system:** When you breathe properly, your body gets more oxygen, which helps improve the efficiency of your cardiovascular system. This means that vital organs are getting the oxygen they need to function properly.

- **Reduced stress and anxiety:** Proper breathing can help reduce stress and anxiety levels, and improve your overall mood and energy levels. Take a deep breath in and feel the tension melt away.

- **Reduced risk of respiratory illnesses:** By breathing properly, you can reduce the risk of respiratory illnesses such as asthma and bronchitis. You can also improve your lung capacity and athletic performance, allowing you to do more and breathe easier.

![So many things to know about breathing arghhhh](/assets/img/resources/breathing-2.jpg)

#### Common dysfunctions that can affect the way we breathe? 

1. Poor posture: This one is easy to spot! Sit up straight and take a deep breath. Now, slouch and try to take a deep breath. Can you feel the difference? Poor posture can lead to shallow breathing and decrease the amount of oxygen that is being taken in. So, next time you catch yourself slouching, sit up straight and take a deep breath!

1. Over-breathing: Take a few quick, shallow breaths. Did you start to feel lightheaded or dizzy? That's because over-breathing can lead to hyperventilation and cause dizziness and lightheadedness. Instead, try taking slow, deep breaths to help regulate your breathing.

1. Weak diaphragm: Place one hand on your chest and the other on your stomach. Take a deep breath in, and notice which hand moves first. If your chest hand moves first, it may indicate weak diaphragm muscles. Weak diaphragm muscles can lead to difficulty taking in deep breaths and decreased oxygen intake. To strengthen your diaphragm muscles, try practicing diaphragmatic breathing.

1. Muscle tension: Take a deep breath in and hold it for a few seconds. Now, exhale and feel your muscles relax. Muscle tension can cause difficulty in taking in deep breaths and increase the difficulty of exhaling. To help relax your muscles, try incorporating stretching and relaxation techniques into your breathing practice.

1. Stress: Take a deep breath in and hold it for a few seconds. Now, exhale slowly and feel your body relax. Stress can cause shallow breathing and increase the difficulty of taking in deep breaths. To reduce stress and improve your breathing, try incorporating relaxation techniques such as meditation or yoga into your daily routine.

By becoming more aware of these common dysfunctions, we can work towards improving our breathing and overall wellbeing. 

![Mechanic of Breathing](/assets/img/resources/breathing-3.jpg)

#### Types of Breathing Methods

There are several types of breathing methods that can be used to improve overall health and well-being. Below are some examples:

- Pursed-lip breathing: This type of breathing involves inhaling deeply through the nose and exhaling slowly through pursed lips. This technique can help regulate breathing and reduce shortness of breath. 

[youtube:7kpJ0QlRss4]

- Box breathing: Box breathing is a technique that involves inhaling deeply through the nose for a count of four, holding the breath for a count of four, exhaling through the mouth for a count of four, and then holding the breath for a count of four before repeating the cycle. This method can help reduce stress and anxiety levels and improve overall breathing. 

[youtube:aPYmZOhJF5Q]

- Wim Hof breathing: This technique involves taking a series of deep breaths and then holding the breath for an extended period of time. This method can help improve oxygen intake and increase energy levels. (Fun fact: Wim Hof holds 21 Guinness world records.)

[youtube:tybOi4hjZFQ]

Each type of breathing method has its own unique benefits. It is important to understand the proper techniques for each type of breathing in order to get the most out of the practice and improve your overall health and well-being.

![Breathe, my friend, just breathe](/assets/img/resources/breathing-4.jpg)

![This is you after doing Wim Hof Breathing ](/assets/img/resources/breathing-5.jpg)

#### Three areas to focus on when it comes to breathing:

1. **Breathing into your stomach and back:** This is also known as diaphragmatic or belly breathing. Inhale deeply and let your belly expand as you breathe in. This engages the diaphragm muscle to pull air into the lungs, allowing you to take deeper breaths and improve the amount of oxygen delivered to your body.

1. **Costal breathing:** This type of breathing involves inhaling into the lower rib cage (intercostal muscles), allowing your rib cage to expand outward. This helps improve lung expansion and can strengthen the muscles in your chest and back.

1. **360 breathing:** Also known as full yogic breathing, this technique involves inhaling deeply and fully expanding your diaphragm. Inhale, allowing your belly to expand, then continue the inhale and let your rib cage expand outward. Finally, continue the inhale and fill your chest with air. As you exhale, release the air from your chest, rib cage, and belly in that order. This can help improve lung capacity and oxygen intake.

By being aware of your breathing capabilities, you can engage muscles and tissue along your midline, which can help dissipate stress more evenly throughout your body.

#### Practice these 3 breathing exercises:

[youtube:bMah6KJlKaY]

1. Supine lying with knees at a 90/90 angle (aim to create intra-abdominal pressure)

[youtube:bMah6KJlKaY]

1. Side lying rib shift (aim to open your rib laterally)

[youtube:HMJeVvU6bMQ]

1. Posterior Expansion breathing exercise

[youtube:n_FWm1W-_28]

#### **Oxygenation: More Than Just Breathing In and Out**

Breathing isn't just about drawing air into and out of our lungs; it's primarily about oxygenation. When we inhale, our lungs absorb oxygen from the air and transfer it to our bloodstream. This oxygen is then distributed to every cell in our body, crucial for cellular function and energy production.

Several factors can affect this process:

- **Health Conditions:** Diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), sleep apnea, and asthma can impact your body's ability to absorb oxygen.

- **Circulation Issues:** Conditions like peripheral artery disease, diabetes, or heart diseases can disrupt the distribution of oxygen-rich blood to all cells.

- **Environmental Factors:** The oxygen content in the air can vary with the environment. For example, at high altitudes, efficient breathing might not supply as much oxygen as at lower levels. Additionally, poor air quality and pollution can hinder effective breathing.

- **Low Hemoglobin Levels:** Hemoglobin, a protein in your red blood cells, binds to oxygen in your lungs and carries it to the rest of your body. If you have low hemoglobin levels (anemia), your body may struggle to transport the oxygen you inhale.

- **Physical Activity Levels:** Regular exercise enhances oxygen utilization, while a sedentary lifestyle can lead to shallow breathing and reduced lung capacity.

By understanding these factors, you can better manage and optimize your body's oxygenation process.

![Yes! you can finally fly!! Feel the wings underneath your lungs](/assets/img/resources/breathing-6.jpg)

Common FAQ (Click the link to open)

**Should you breathe through your nose or mouth?**

It is recommended to breathe through your nose whenever possible. Nasal breathing helps filter, moisturize, and heat up the air, reducing the amount of dust, bacteria, viruses, etc. that enter the body. Additionally, nasal breathing helps send air to the bottom of the lungs, which are bigger and connected to the parasympathetic system. In contrast, mouth breathing can dry out your mouth and throat. Proper, calm, controlled, and rhythmic breathing can improve lung capacity.

**If you or your partner snores while sleeping**

Yes, snoring can be a sign of bad breathing. It can indicate that the airway is partially blocked, which can lead to shallow or interrupted breathing. This can result in a lack of oxygen and poor quality sleep.

**Suggestions to Improve Breathing**

- Mouth tape

- Neti pot or nasal spray

- Consultation with an otolaryngologist or ENT specialist

- Improving air quality (Air purifier)

**What are some common symptoms of poor breathing?**

Symptoms can vary for each individual, but they often include shortness of breath, rapid breathing, chest pain or discomfort, lightheadedness, and frequent yawning or sighing.

**Can I improve my breathing technique?**

Yes, with practice and correct methods, you can enhance your breathing. Techniques such as diaphragmatic breathing, pursed-lip breathing, and box breathing can all help. Adding my three favorite positions can also facilitate the intercostal breathing muscle to work effectively.

**How does stress affect my breathing?**

Stress can alter your breathing pattern, leading to more rapid and shallow breaths. This can disrupt the muscle coordination between your intercostal muscles, diaphragm, and scalene muscles. If left unchecked, this can cause hyperventilation, leading to symptoms like dizziness, lightheadedness, and in severe cases, fainting.

**Can diet affect my breathing?**

Yes, a healthy diet can support lung health. Foods rich in antioxidants, such as fruits and vegetables, can help protect your lungs from damage. On the other hand, a diet high in processed foods and unhealthy fats can lead to inflammation and harm your lung health.

resources.body:
### **Adopt a Fixed Schedule/Routine:**

Consistency is crucial for achieving your fitness goals. A fixed schedule allows your body to adapt to the routine, gradually enhancing your performance and outcomes.

![Example 1](/assets/img/resources/session-preparation-1.jpg)

![Screenshot of David Gray's Rehab protocol (top rehab program template)](/assets/img/resources/session-preparation-2.jpg)

![Andrew Hubermans’ fitness protocol (Neuroscientist popular for his advice for longevity)](/assets/img/resources/session-preparation-3.jpg)

![Peter Attia’s exercise routine (physician, and researcher known for his work in longevity medicine)](/assets/img/resources/session-preparation-4.jpg)

Here are three individuals renowned for their extensive knowledge in health and wellness. Their deep commitment to fitness and health makes them inspiring role models. Don't worry if your current routine doesn't align with theirs. The purpose of sharing these examples is to learn from the best, understand how to maximize our time for fitness, and enhance our daily productivity. Remember, it's always a work in progress. If you don't have a routine yet, it's time to establish one!

![If you fail to plan ](/assets/img/resources/session-preparation-5.jpg)

### Effective Lifestyle Planning

If you've been training with me, you'll notice that I ask three key questions before we start our session:

1. **How's your sleep?** Sleep is essential for optimal performance and overall health, as it's the period when your body recovers and rebuilds muscle tissues worked during exercise.

1. **How's your nutrition over the last few days?** Your diet fuels your workouts and aids in recovery and adaptation. The quality of your meals directly influences your energy levels and performance.

1. **Are you feeling any pain today?** Understanding your current physical state helps me customize the session to avoid aggravating any issues, ensuring your workout is safe and effective.

For better results and performance, and to age stronger, we need to optimize our routines outside the gym. Good sleep, nutrition, and recovery routines are essential to prevent obstacles that could slow down our results.

[https://giphy.com/gifs/baby-tired-falling-asleep-lSxpaFCtsOUpfiBYUV](https://giphy.com/gifs/baby-tired-falling-asleep-lSxpaFCtsOUpfiBYUV)

### Optimizing Our Sessions

To make the most of our time together, please choose from the following three session types. Let me know your preference in advance, especially if it requires booking the treatment area. This will ensure a smoother treatment and exercise flow for optimal results. 

![](/assets/img/resources/session-preparation-6.jpg)

![](/assets/img/resources/session-preparation-7.jpg)

![](/assets/img/resources/session-preparation-8.jpg)

- **1hr Manual Therapy:** This is ideal for those experiencing discomfort at a level of 3/10 or above, or for those who want therapeutic work for optimizing body alignment. This is not a massage session, but a combination of osteopathic techniques, manual therapy, and manual muscle activation to balance your body.

- **1hr Strength Conditioning:** Perfect for refining techniques and forms, and focusing on specific exercises to enhance muscle growth and improve posture.

- **Combined Therapy:** A balanced 1-hour session with 30 minutes of manual therapy and 30 minutes of physical therapy. This is the best option if you're experiencing minor discomfort (below 2/10) that you want to eliminate permanently.

Note: If necessary, we can extend our session by an additional 30 minutes (please inform me beforehand).

> Note For the Advanced: To achieve more, consider dedicating 15 minutes before or after the session to complete necessary homework!

![Let's go! Your commitment are key to our success.](/assets/img/resources/session-preparation-9.jpg)

resources.title: The Quest for the Best Supplements
resources.summary: An honest look at what's legit, what's hype, and how to make smarter supplement choices, from creatine and omega-3 to greens powders and fat burners.
resources.body:
![](/assets/img/resources/best-supplements-1.jpg)

## **🧠 The Quest for the Best Supplements**

#### **What’s legit, what’s hype, and how to make smarter choices for your health & performance**

---

![We are all looking for that magic spinach… Too bad we aren’t **Popeye**](/assets/img/resources/best-supplements-2.jpg)

---

### **🧭 Why I Even Bothered With This**

When you're serious about optimizing your health not just looking fit, but *functioning* at a high level supplements always sneak into the conversation.

Every second post on your feed seems to be someone mixing a green powder, holding a capsule like it's the cure to modern life, or quoting Andrew Huberman like scripture. I'll admit, I got pulled in too. I've tried AG1, IM-8, the so-called "ultimate biohacker stacks," and yeah, some of them helped.

My energy felt smoother. A few blood markers improved. But after a while, I started wondering:

> "Is this actually helping me… or am I just paying for expensive pee?"

So I decided to go down the rabbit hole pulling research, talking to other coaches, listening to nerdy podcasts, and using ChatGPT like my supplement research assistant on steroids (metaphorically speaking 😏).

>  This page is the result of that journey. No sales pitch. No affiliate links. Just an honest look at what works, what's overhyped, and how you can stop burning cash on supplements that don't move the needle.

---

### **🔍 The Supplement World is Noisy**

Let’s be real. The supplement industry is a multi-billion dollar beast. And while some products are backed by decades of research, others are just slick branding wrapped around underdosed blends.

You’ve got:

- 🧪 *Lab-tested essentials* (creatine, omega-3s, D3… legit stuff)

- 🌿 *Green powders that promise miracles but taste like pond water*

- 💊 *Multivitamins that look like they could power Iron Man’s arc reactor*

So how do we know what’s worth it?

That’s where I break it down.

---

### **✅ Supplements That Actually Deliver**

#### **1️⃣ Creatine Monohydrate**

If I could only recommend one supplement to almost everyone—athletes, weekend warriors, even your parents it'd be this.

🧠 Supports **strength, power, recovery**, and even **cognitive performance**

💰 **Safe, affordable**, and backed by hundreds of clinical studies

💡 **Best form**: Creapure® or micronized monohydrate

📏 **Dose**: 3–5g daily (no need to load or cycle)

⚠️ **Myth**: It does *not* damage kidneys in healthy individuals

---

#### **2️⃣ Omega-3 (EPA/DHA)**

Omega-3 fatty acids are essential for **brain, heart, joint health**, and **inflammation control** — especially if you don’t eat fatty fish regularly.

💡 **Look for**: Triglyceride form, IFOS-certified, wild-caught sourcing

📏 **Dose**: ~1,000–2,000 mg combined EPA/DHA per day

🐟 **Reality**: Krill oil is pricier but not significantly better for most people

---

#### **3️⃣ Protein Powder (Isolate or Plant-Based Blend)**

*Whole food always comes first but unless you meal prep like a bodybuilder, hitting your daily protein goal can be a struggle.* That’s where a clean protein powder helps

💡 **Choose**: Whey isolate or hydrolysate for better digestion and higher leucine

🧪 **Bonus**: Look for Informed-Sport, Labdoor-tested products, or minimal ingredients

🧀 **Tip**: Lactose-sensitive? Go for isolate or a good plant-based option

---

#### **4️⃣ High-Quality Multivitamin**

Most multis are either poorly absorbed or underdosed. But a **well-formulated** one can help bridge real nutritional gaps especially in high-stress, active lifestyles.

💡 **Look for**:

- Methylated B vitamins (e.g. B12 as methylcobalamin)

- Chelated minerals (e.g. magnesium glycinate)

- Transparent labels (no proprietary blends)

🚫 **Avoid**: Gummy multis (often low potency and high in sugar)

---

### **❌ What’s Mostly Hype**

#### **💚 Greens Powders (AG1, IM-8, etc.)**

They *look* great on Instagram and feel like an insurance policy but don’t overestimate them.

🧪 Some offer gut or adaptogen benefits, but usually in low or unclear doses

⚠️ Most are proprietary blends, making it hard to verify efficacy

💸 ~S$3–4/serving ≠ better than a plate of real greens

---

#### **🧪 Collagen**

Collagen has its place especially for skin, joints, and connective tissue support but it’s not a miracle supplement.

📉 **Not ideal for muscle building** low in leucine and incomplete as a protein

📏 Needs 10–20g/day (preferably with Vitamin C) for noticeable benefits

🧃 Best taken on an empty stomach or away from complete proteins (to avoid absorption competition)

---

#### **🔥 Fat Burners & Detox Teas**

These are usually loaded with **caffeine, diuretics**, and **appetite suppressants** not real fat-burning magic.

🧯 No tea “detoxes” your liver your liver already does that

🧪 Most fat burners are no better than a strong coffee

💸 Save your cash. Prioritize sleep, training, and a sustainable routine

---

### **🧪 My Research Process (tap tap tap…)**

![](/assets/img/resources/best-supplements-3.jpg)

I used GPT + evidence-based sources to sort through:

- Ingredient quality

- Clinical dosages (not just label claims)

- 3rd-party testing (NSF, Informed-Sport, IFOS)

- Absorption and practicality

- Price per serving vs. value

Then I compared the **top 10 products** in each category available in **Singapore**, so this isn’t just U.S.-centric fluff.

You can explore the full comparison tables here:

| **🔗 **[**Multivitamin Comparison**](https://chatgpt.com/share/686b1fd9-f0cc-8011-95de-7c3a32676652) | **🔗 **[**Protein Comparison**](https://chatgpt.com/share/686be627-319c-8011-b981-0f261ca6b377) |

| --- | --- |

| 🔗 [Omega-3 Comparison](https://chatgpt.com/share/686be60b-0c84-8011-b8fc-af76b25cd26f) | 🔗 [Creatine Comparison](https://chatgpt.com/share/686be645-abac-8011-a792-d82019a873cd) |

---

### **🏆 My Personal Top Picks (No Sponsorships)**

| **Category** | **My Pick** | **Why** |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Creatine | **Thorne or Klean Athlete** | Clean, pure, tested |

| Omega-3 | **WHC UnoCardio or Nordic Naturals** | High EPA/DHA, low oxidation |

| Protein | **Transparent Labs Whey Isolate** | Mixes well, high leucine, grass-fed |

| Multi | **Life Extension Mix** | Potent, broad-spectrum support |

| Budget Multi | **Pure Encapsulations or Garden of Life** | Gentle, solid coverage |

---

### **⚠️ Final Reminders**

>

**Key Supplement Wisdom:**

- **More isn't always better.** You don't need 10 different powders to be healthy.

- **You're not broken.** But you might be nutrient-deficient.

- **Always cross-check with your doctor or dietitian,** especially if you're on meds or have underlying health issues.

- **Supplements can help, but habits still win.**

---

### **🌱 Foundations First**

>

**Before buying your 14th supplement this month, ask yourself:**

- 🍎 Are you eating real, nutrient-dense food?

- 💪 Training consistently with proper form (preferably under the loving torture of a ReGen Performance Coach 😏)

- 😴 Getting 7-9 hours of quality sleep?

- 🧘 Actively managing your stress levels?

If these foundations aren't dialed in, no supplement can save you. But once they are the right additions can absolutely give you an edge.

Need personalized guidance? We’re happy to help you create a supplement strategy that complements your lifestyle and goals. Just reach out!

Let's build something that actually works for *you*.
